subject: Request: temporary SLA exception & on-call escalation plan for Finlytics migration
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@finlytics.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Upcoming data migration week — potential P1 spike & request for temporary SLA exception

Hi Aditya + Ben,

We have a scheduled platform migration in our environment the week of Sep 6 that could cause a transient increase in incident volume (expected bump in P1/P2 pageings while we stabilize cached traffic). Our SRE team estimates a 24–36 hour window of elevated risk during cutover and the downstream 24 hours for regression fixes.

Can Redwood provide a temporary amendment to the standard P1/P2 response commitments for the following window: Sep 6 22:00 UTC through Sep 8 22:00 UTC? Specifically we would like: 
- P1 response SLA: 60 minutes (temporary, normally 30)
- P2 response SLA: 4 hours (temporary, normally 2)

We understand this is an exception and are prepared to accept tighter escalation rules and an agreed runbook. Attached is our migration-plan.pdf and the migration timeline. Please let us know what you need (runbook, on-call coverage, credit language) to move this forward.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
VP, Platform Engineering
Finlytics

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@finlytics.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@finlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming data migration week — potential P1 spike & request for temporary SLA exception

Thanks Elena — got the plan and timeline. We can support a temporary exception but need to formalize:
- explicit start/end times (UTC)
- an approved escalation runbook and a named on-call rotation with contacts
- agreement on credit or fee adjustments in case of unplanned degradations

laura (support manager) — can you draft a narrowly scoped runbook and confirm on-call availability for Sep 6–8? Ben — heads up on credit/contract angle; we may need a short amendment.

Ill put together a draft SLA-exception-form for signatures and open a Jira (INF-1294) to track approvals.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Elena Morales <elena@finlytics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@finlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Sep 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming data migration week — potential P1 spike & request for temporary SLA exception

Elena — appreciate the heads up. From a commercial perspective, a temporary SLA amendment is fine. Two asks: 
1) We will require a written runbook and named SRE contacts that Redwood can escalate to during the window.
2) If theres an outage meeting our P1 definition that isn't caused by the migration plan itself, we should limit credits to an agreed cap (I propose 10% of monthly invoice pro-rated for the exception window).

Aditya — Ill prepare a short amendment (SLA-exception-form.docx) and route to legal/procurement. Laura — can you confirm support headcount and ensure we have on-call overlap for the nights of Sep 6 and Sep 7 (US overnight coverage)?

Thanks — happy to hop on a 15-min call to finalize.

—Ben
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Elena Morales <elena@finlytics.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finlytics.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming data migration week — proposed runbook & on-call rota

Hi all,

Attached is runbook-draft.md (high level) and a proposed on-call rota for Sep 6–8. Key points: 
- Redwood will maintain standard P1 Pager duty; for the exception window well add a second senior engineer on overlap shifts (23:00–07:00 UTC) to shorten triage handoff time.
- Escalation path (summary): engineer -> on-call lead -> Support Manager (Laura Bennett) -> Head of CS (Aditya Rao). For incidents impacting >50% of Finlytics customers we will escalate immediately to Director-level and schedule a bridge.
- Communication cadence: 1) immediate Slack alert, 2) status email every 60 minutes for active P1s, 3) post-mortem within 72 hours.

Please review the runbook for any missing steps. If Finlytics signs off I will attach the runbook to the SLA-exception-form and route for signatures.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Support Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: runbook-draft.md (text), SLA-exception-form.docx (draft)

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@finlytics.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@finlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming data migration week — final: SLA exception approval & next steps

Elena — thanks for the quick coordination. Summary of agreement and next steps: 
1) Exception window: 2026-09-06T22:00:00Z through 2026-09-08T22:00:00Z.
2) Temporary SLAs: P1 response target 60 minutes, P2 response target 4 hours. These revert to standard terms after the window.
3) Escalation runbook: attached (runbook-draft.md) — Finlytics to confirm SRE contacts by EOD Sep 8.
4) Commercials: Ben will circulate SLA-exception-form.docx to your procurement/legal for sign-off. Proposed credit cap: 10% pro-rated for the window.
5) Tracking: Jira INF-1294 created for approvals and post-mortem tracking; please add any internal Finlytics tickets there.

Elena — please confirm acceptance by replying and well start the DocuSign flow. We will also request a one-hour dry-run channel test on Sep 5 UTC to ensure alerting and bridges work.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference
